title: The Brown adjoint of $Rf_!$ on the localizing category

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal T_X$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal T_Y$. Since $Y$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes it qcqs. For each chosen $c=(j,p)$, [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] gives an exact, direct-sum-preserving restriction $F_c=Rp_*D(j_!):\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. The source Brown structures and compact generators are assumed; [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] at $Y$ supplies a locally small triangulated target with direct sums. All sums use the fixed indexing universe.

By [lem-pc-brown-hom-representability-locally-small], step 1 gives representability of $M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(F_cM,N)$ for each $N$ in the fixed universe. Apply [lem-sfb-right-adjoint-from-objectwise-representability] to assemble a functor $G_c$ and the natural adjunction bijections $F_c\dashv G_c$. Set $f_c^!=G_c$, proving clause (1).

source.place: Tag 0A8G, proposition-brown proof, using Categories Tag 0A8B, lemma-adjoint-exists.

proof.text: For $F_c\dashv G_c$, [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] (iii) equips $G_c$ with coherent integer-shift isomorphisms compatible with both unit and counit. Its uniqueness clause identifies these as the adjunction-induced shifts.
Apply [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] to step 1 and the compatible shifts of step 3. It makes $G_c$ exact with those shifts, proving clause (2).

For another right adjoint $J$ of $F_c$, [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] gives the unique counit-compatible isomorphism $\gamma:G_c\cong J$. For $a:M\to G_cN$, its $J$-transpose after $\gamma_N$ is $\varepsilon^J_N F_c(\gamma_N a)=\varepsilon^c_N F_c(a)$. Thus this is precisely compatibility with all adjunction bijections, proving the first assertion of clause (3).

source.place: Part (3): uniqueness for a fixed compactification

proof.text: For all compactifications, [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] gives the canonical $\phi_{ji}:F_i\cong F_j$ with identity and cocycle laws. Apply [lem-sfb-coherent-right-adjoint-comparisons] to the adjunctions from step 2. It supplies the unique $\gamma_{ji}:G_i\cong G_j$ normalized by $\varepsilon^j_N F_j(\gamma_{ji,N})=\varepsilon^i_N\phi_{ji,G_iN}^{-1}$, identifies all adjunction bijections, and gives identity and cocycle laws. This proves compactification independence in clause (3).

source.place: Part (3), last sentence: transfer along the compactification isomorphism and compatibility with the cocycle condition; general categorical form of the comparison argument.
